reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Probability.markedPredictableSigma
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: P (x) calE, the product of the predictable sigma-field on (time) x Omega with the
mark sigma-algebra. Faithful Lean: the sigma-algebra generated by markedPredictableRect, or the
product sigma-algebra of predictableSigma with the measurable space of E (equal, since products
of generators generate the product sigma-algebra when each generating family contains a
countable cover, which the rectangles do: (0,n] x Omega, E). Caveats on the time-0 slice as for
predictableSigma.

comparison.text:
Lean: markedPredictableSigma F nu := generateFrom (markedPredictableRect F nu) on Omega x R x E.
Comparison with the locked reading: on Omega x (0,inf) x E this is P|_{(0,inf)} (x) calE: the
rectangles F' x (r,q] (0 <= r, F' in F r) generate the predictable sigma-field on (0,inf), the
finite-mass mark sets generate calE for sigma-finite nu (every B is a countable union of B cap S_k
with S_k the spanning sets), and products of generating families containing countable covers
generate the product sigma-algebra. It is contained in the product sigma-algebra
(markedPredictableSigma_le), and every predictable set cut at times <= t is F t (x) Borel (x)
calE-measurable (measurableSet_inter_timeIic). Difference (as for the rectangles): no initial
cell; Omega x (-inf,0] x E is an atom, so the time-0 slice is trivial instead of F_0 (x) calE.
Representation choices: (1) missing time-0 cell (harmless up to dt x dP x nu-null sets, see
markedPredictableRect); (2) dependence on nu through its finite-mass sets (no dependence for the
paper's sigma-finite nu); (3) time axis R, order Omega x R x E.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: (1) mark sets restricted to finite nu-mass (generates the same
sigma-algebra for the paper's sigma-finite nu); (2) no time-0 cell {0} x A x B (A in F_0) and no
rectangle at times <= 0, so the generated sigma-algebra has the region of times <= 0 as an atom -
harmless because time 0 is dt-null and the paper identifies jump integrands up to
dt x dP x nu-null sets; (3) generators F' x (r,q] x B with F' in F r, r >= 0: the standard
left-open predictable rectangles; order Omega x R x E.
On Omega x (0,inf) x E the generated sigma-algebra is P|_{(0,inf)} (x) calE (products of
generating families with countable covers), contained in the product sigma-algebra
(markedPredictableSigma_le).
